extra.reason: Fixed in caa7df1: TYPE-OF now returns KEYWORD for keyword symbols, matching SBCL/CLHS. TYPEP+SUBTYPEP already agreed.

Fixed in ba9366e: added has-user-fill-pointer flag as COMPLEX_ARRAY body word 4, threaded from MAKE-ARRAY through %make-complex-vector. ARRAY-HAS-FILL-POINTER-P now matches SBCL on all cases; ADJUST-ARRAY heuristic (bliss-6wng) dropped.

Fixed in 49cf132. Confirmed real: a nursery COMPLEX_ARRAY relocates on its first minor GC, and the pre-fix code wrote the new storage/fill-pointer to the stale address (regression test fails pre-fix with fill-pointer 0 instead of 1). Fix roots v/value AND hoists build_vector out of the argument list (arg-eval order reloaded *v before the alloc). New test: crates/bliss-stdlib/tests/complex_vector_gc.rs. No write barrier needed - minor_gc scans survivor->nursery edges.

Fixed in 1bfa7fb. The bead title was stale (single-segment ~mincol<> already right-justified); the real bugs were (a) logical blocks keyed on the opening ~:< instead of the closing ~:>, so ~10:<abc~> emitted 'abc' unpadded and multi-segment ~:</~:@< crashed on ~;, and (b) justification ignored :/@ modifiers, colinc and minpad. SBCL on this box supplied the reference oracle the bead was waiting for: 27 justification cases + logical-block forms now byte-identical to SBCL, locked in as tests in crates/bliss-stdlib/tests/test_format.rs.

Done in 866d58f. Confirmed the two consumers did NOT share a source of truth: deopt derived a Rebox from each slot's ValueRepresentation, while the emit OSR stub destructured ValueSource::Value{value, ..} and discarded the representation entirely, moving a raw word from the interpreter frame; osr::ConversionKind had no constructor tying it to ValueRepresentation and no F32/F64 split where Rebox has both. Added t2/slot_map.rs as the single producer; both sides now read it. Added ConversionKind::for_repr as the inverse of Rebox::for_repr (None for UnboxedF64, which D4.09's vocabulary cannot express). emit now DECLINES an OSR entry whose slots need any conversion rather than emitting a wrong one. Guard tests: (a) import/export inverses for every representation, (b) tests/osr_deopt_slot_agreement.rs asserts slot count + locals/stack split + per-slot repr agree at a real captured safepoint. Verified non-vacuous by temporarily recording UnboxedFixnum in build_frame_state: agreement test still passes (shared producer works), Tagged guard fails with exact slot+bcp.

INVALID — my own measurement error, retracting. The UnsupportedOp(0xF5) I recorded was caused by a TEMPORARY experimental edit I still had in the tree (build_frame_state patched to record ValueRepresentation::UnboxedFixnum, to prove the bliss-ht4 guards were non-vacuous). Two of the three 0xF5 sites (emit.rs:1257 and :2753) are exactly 'frame-state slot repr != Tagged' refusals in the deopt-metadata emission path, so my flip tripped them.

On clean code the loop compiles and OSR IS emitted. Measured with BLISS_T2_LOG=stderr BLISS_T2_THRESHOLD=3 on the same (defun hot (n) ... tagbody ... go top ...) loop:

  [T2] HOT: speculated 3 site(s)
  PROBE EMITTED OSR entry bcp=5 offset=1409      <- temporary probe in the emission loop
  [T2] HOT: T2 INSTALLED - 1449 bytes, spill_slots=7, gc_shadow_slots=3, safepoints=2

So the OSR-entry emission path is live and reachable for tagbody/Go loops; there is no bail to fix. bliss-izt.4 (backward Br gets no OSR entry at all) was measured on clean code and still stands.

Useful residue for bliss-fjz: emit.rs:1257 and :2753 already REFUSE any frame-state slot whose repr is not Tagged, which is why an unboxed frame state fails emit before OSR is reached. The OSR-side decline added in 866d58f is the counterpart of those two refusals, so when bliss-fjz teaches deopt to rebox unboxed slots and lifts them, OSR does not silently become the weak link.

Done in df34bb9, but the bead's PREMISE WAS WRONG and I am correcting it. I claimed DO/DOTIMES/DOLIST never get an OSR entry because they lower to Br. They do not: lower_dotimes (cli/bytecode.rs ~2291) expands to (GO top), so they were already captured. My evidence for the bead was a synthetic hand-written bytecode probe using Instr::Br(2); I generalised it to real lowering without checking, the same mistake as bliss-izt.5.

Measured before/after osr_entries counts over dotimes/do/dolist/tagbody/nested/cons/early/string/loop-for/loop-while: IDENTICAL (L-DOTIMES 1, L-DOLIST 1, L-TAGBODY 1, L-NESTED 2, L-LOOP 1). The change fixes no loop that exists today.

Kept anyway as robustness: the OSR safety condition is that the TARGET has entry_depth == 0, which is a property of the target rather than of the jumping instruction, so capture_osr_entries is now instruction-agnostic (Go/Br/BrIfFalse/BrIfTrue). A future lowering emitting a backward Br now gets an OSR entry automatically instead of silently getting none. Guarded by every_backward_branch_shape_yields_an_osr_safepoint in tests/osr_deopt_slot_agreement.rs.

Genuinely useful side-effect: T2 INSTALLED now logs osr_entries=N. OSR coverage was previously invisible from outside the emitter, which is why the wrong premise survived; the log is what disproved it. Recommend using it when working bliss-izt/bliss-wen4.

Also found while validating this: bliss-wc4t (PUSH in a loop => 'unbound variable: CONS' under BLISS_GC_STRESS, deterministic, T2-independent).
